summary: Describes how GIST can use SCTP and DTLS for connection mode operation, where it currently uses TCP or TLS over TCP. It is experimental.

eli5.summary: GIST sends signaling messages over TCP. This lets it use another delivery method, SCTP, with encryption on top.

subtitle: How GIST signaling can run over SCTP and be secured with DTLS instead of TCP and TLS.

tldr.problem: GIST connection mode ran over TCP or TLS over TCP, which brings head-of-line blocking, strict ordering and no multihoming, while some signaling messages have a limited lifetime.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC adds an MA-Protocol-ID for SCTP (value 3) and one for DTLS (value 4), and explains how to use SCTP streams, PR-SCTP timed reliability and multihoming.
tldr.outcome: It is an Experimental RFC, and the unit metadata shows it is updated by RFC 8996.

today: RFC 6084 is an Experimental RFC and the unit metadata shows it is updated by RFC 8996. The RFC itself describes GIST over SCTP and DTLS as an experiment for examination and evaluation.

sections.title: Why GIST Over SCTP
sections.content:
GIST connection mode (C-mode) originally ran on a reliable, in-order byte stream, using TCP. But some NSLP (Next Steps in Signaling Signaling Layer Protocol) context information has a definite lifetime, so stale messages held up by congestion could be dropped rather than retransmitted.

The RFC points to head-of-line blocking and multihoming issues in TCP. SCTP also offers reliability, congestion control and fragmentation, plus multiple streams, multiple IP addresses and message orientation, which removes the need for separate framing. Its Partial Reliability extension (PR-SCTP) allows partial retransmission based on a programmable timer. DTLS provides a way to secure SCTP.

No change to the high-level operation of GIST is needed. SCTP implementations used for GIST MUST support fragmentation of SCTP user messages.
sections.eli5: The old delivery truck makes every parcel wait if one gets stuck. The new service has several lanes, so one stuck parcel does not hold up the others.

sections.title: Forwards-SCTP and State Handling
sections.content:
The base GIST specification defines Forwards-TCP and TLS as messaging association protocols. This RFC adds Forwards-SCTP (value 3). As with Forwards-TCP, the querying node opens the connection towards the responder. Support is OPTIONAL. If offered, MA-protocol-options data MUST also be in the SCD object: nothing but the field header in a Query, and in a Response a 2-byte port number followed by 2 pad bytes. The destination address comes from the Network-Layer-Information object and the port from the SCD object.

Implementations MUST set up both downstream and upstream SCTP streams with the same stream identifier, forming a bidirectional stream. All GIST messages of one session MUST use the same SCTP stream so the NSLP can assume in-order delivery. Several sessions MAY share a stream under local policy. Errors such as an SCTP reset MUST be reported to NSLPs.
sections.eli5: The one who starts the chat calls the other side on a number they were given. All messages about one conversation stay in the same lane so they arrive in order.

sections.title: PR-SCTP, Multihoming and Streams
sections.content:
An SCTP implementation for GIST SHOULD try to set up a PR-SCTP association with the "timed reliability" service if available. With ordinary reliable delivery, a message already transmitted once before its lifetime expires must be sent as a normal reliable message, which wastes bandwidth during congestion. Timed reliability avoids this and is RECOMMENDED. The Timeout parameter of the API call SendMessage is used as the PR-SCTP timeout.

If SCTP detects failure of the primary path, GIST SHOULD tell the NSLP using NetworkNotification with type "Routing Status Change", even if multihoming kept the connection open.

Multihoming is of limited use for the default path-coupled routing method, since a failed path probably also fails the signaled traffic. Streams help because different sessions can use different streams, so a loss in one does not block the others.
sections.eli5: If a note is only useful for a short time, the sender can give up on it instead of sending it again late. If the main road is closed, the service can try a side road and tell the sender.

sections.title: DTLS With GIST
sections.content:
A new MA-Protocol-ID, DTLS (value 4), secures GIST, initially together with SCTP. It provides server authentication and integrity (unless the NULL ciphersuite is chosen), and optionally replay protection for control packets. Using DTLS to secure GIST over datagram transports MUST be implemented and SHOULD be used.

Implementations MUST NOT negotiate versions earlier than DTLS v1.0 and MUST use the highest version both peers support. NULL authentication and integrity ciphers MUST NOT be negotiated, though confidentiality can use NULL ciphersuites. Renegotiation is RECOMMENDED to be disabled. DTLS needs no MA-protocol-options of its own, because the transport underneath (for example the SCTP port) supplies them.

The security considerations of GIST, SCTP and DTLS apply. SCTP's own replay protection is expected to protect NSIS messages carried over DTLS over SCTP.
sections.eli5: DTLS is a lockable envelope for the notes. The envelope is always checked for tampering, and the old, weak lock styles are not allowed.

sections.title: IANA Codepoints
sections.content:
IANA registered two MA-Protocol-IDs in the registry created by the GIST specification: 3 for SCTP opened in the forwards direction and 4 for DTLS initiated in the forwards direction. DTLS is never used alone. It is always paired with a transport protocol named in the stack proposal.

NAT traversal follows the GIST specification and its extensibility capabilities. This RFC defines no NAT traversal procedures for SCTP.
sections.eli5: Two new numbered slots were added to an official list, one for the delivery service and one for the envelope.

fields.name: SCTP port number
fields.desc: Port at which the responder accepts SCTP connections; only supplied by the responder.

items.label: SCTP
items.desc: SCTP opened in the forwards direction.

items.label: DTLS
items.desc: DTLS initiated in the forwards direction; always coupled with a transport protocol.
